o: We aggregate orders per customer and filter groups by four conditions: at least 3 orders, at least 60% of orders in peak windows (11:00–14:00 or 18:00–21:00), average rating of rated orders at least 4.0 rounded to 2 decimals, and at least half the orders rated. Customer 101 passes with 4 orders, 100% peak, rating 4.67; customer 102 fails on rating (3.5); customer 104 fails on peak percentage; customers 103 and 105 pass. Ordering is by average_rating DESC then customer_id DESC.
k: Flag peak hours per row with a CASE expression, then aggregate.
Use HAVING for group-level filters and ROUND for display precision.

a.i: Compute an is_peak flag per order in a subquery, then GROUP BY customer_id and apply all four business rules in HAVING. COUNT(order_rating) naturally ignores NULLs, giving the rated-order ratio for free.
s: Derive is_peak = 1 when TIME(order_timestamp) falls in [11:00,14:00) or [18:00,21:00).
Group by customer_id; count orders and rated orders.
Filter in HAVING: count >= 3, peak ratio >= 0.6, AVG(rating) >= 4.0, rated ratio >= 0.5.
Order by average_rating DESC, customer_id DESC.

c.python:
SELECT customer_id,
       COUNT(*) AS total_orders,
       ROUND(100 * SUM(is_peak) / COUNT(*)) AS peak_hour_percentage,
       ROUND(AVG(order_rating), 2) AS average_rating
FROM (
  SELECT *,
         CASE WHEN (TIME(order_timestamp) >= '11:00:00' AND TIME(order_timestamp) < '14:00:00')
                OR (TIME(order_timestamp) >= '18:00:00' AND TIME(order_timestamp) < '21:00:00')
              THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_peak
  FROM restaurant_orders
) t
GROUP BY customer_id
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3
   AND SUM(is_peak) / COUNT(*) >= 0.6
   AND AVG(order_rating) >= 4.0
   AND COUNT(order_rating) / COUNT(*) >= 0.5
ORDER BY average_rating DESC, customer_id DESC;

w: The boundary semantics of the peak windows matter: use half-open intervals [11:00,14:00) and [18:00,21:00) so 14:01 and 21:00 are excluded consistently. Common pitfalls: dividing integer counts (cast or rely on decimal division), forgetting NULL ratings in AVG (AVG skips NULLs automatically, which is what we want), and rounding before filtering (filter on the raw average). Follow-ups: peak hours varying by day of week, or weighting by order_amount.
